I'll read the lavish skill file so I can answer from the source, not just the summary.

Yes. I have access to **lavish**.

**Where:** `/Users/sinchunyeung/github/.agents/skills/lavish/SKILL.md` (workspace skill under `.agents/skills/lavish/`).

**What it does:** It turns plans, comparisons, diagrams, tables, diffs, reports, and similar content into reviewable HTML, opened via the `lavish-axi` CLI (`npx -y lavish-axi`). You can annotate the page and send feedback back to the agent. Live workflow/design guidance comes from the CLI (`--help`, `design`, `playbook`), not from the skill file itself.

**Automatic use?** Partially. It is listed in my available skills, and I am supposed to reach for it when a visual artifact would beat prose. It is not a hard auto-trigger on every message. You can also force it with `/lavish` (with an optional description of what the artifact should show).

content.text:
Yes - for the open **Agent Skills** ecosystem (`npx skills` / [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/)), that path is standard.

**Why it’s under `github/.agents`:**  
`lavish` was installed as a **project** skill in your workspace (`/Users/sinchunyeung/github`). The Skills CLI puts those here:

| Scope | Path |
|--------|------|
| Project | `<project>/.agents/skills/<name>/` |
| Global | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` |

Your global ones (`find-skills`, `gh-axi`, etc.) live under `~/.agents/skills/`. Project `lavish` is under `github/.agents/skills/`.

**Is it a standard search location?**  
Yes for Cursor when skills are installed that way. Cursor also loads other skill roots, including:

- `~/.cursor/skills/` and `.cursor/skills/` - Cursor’s own create-skill convention
- `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` - built-in Cursor skills (don’t put yours there)
- Agent-specific dirs the CLI may also target (Claude, OpenCode, etc.)

So `.agents/skills` is the **cross-agent / skills.sh** layout. Cursor’s docs still emphasize `.cursor/skills` for hand-written skills, but Cursor clearly discovers `.agents/skills` too - that’s why `lavish` showed up in this session.
